description:
We are POWER10 - named for NASA POWER API x Uganda's 10 farming zones. We are a team of Ugandan builders passionate about using satellite data to solve real farm problems.

We are building Rota - an app that gives every village its own crop rotation advice using live NASA POWER satellite data. No more generic advice.
summary: RotaUganda - Field Shift transforms NASA satellite data into practical planting decisions for Ugandan smallholders. Many farmers plant the same crop yearly, degrading soil and wasting water. Our web app solves this. Farmers enter location, last crop, and goal (improve soil, save water, increase income). The app calls NASA POWER API live for daily rainfall and temperature for their zone, calculates 10-year climate trends, and uses an anti-monocrop rotation engine to recommend the best next crop with evidence: Example., after maize, beans fix 40kg nitrogen and save 38% water. It includes local context, disclaimers to confirm with extension officers, and responsible AI transparency. It addresses the "Field Shift: Don't Plant the Same" challenge by making NASA data actionable for 80% of Ugandans who depend on farming, crucial as Northern Uganda faces -8% rainfall and +1.1°C warming. It supports climate adaptation, soil health, and food security.
details:
RotaUganda - Field Shift is a web app that tells farmers what to plant next instead of planting the same crop every season.

How it works in three steps:

1. Farmer selects location (10 zones in Northern Uganda), last season's crop (maize, beans, etc), and goal (improve soil, save water, increase income).

2. App calls NASA POWER API live (https://power.larc.nasa.gov/api/temporal/daily/point?parameters=PRECTOTCORR,T2M&community=AG) to get last 30 days rainfall and temperature for that zone, calculates climate trend (-8% rainfall, +1.1°C warming in Gulu).

3. Our anti-monocrop rotation engine checks soil family, blocks same family (no maize after maize), scores crops: legumes get +40kg nitrogen fix for "improve soil", low-water crops save 38% water, market value for income. Shows top three with evidence, disclaimers, and extension officer validation.

Benefits: Prevents soil depletion - after maize, recommends beans/cowpeas that fix 40kg nitrogen/hectare, reducing fertilizer need. Saves water - drought-tolerant crops use 38% less water, critical as rainfall drops 8%. Increases income - factors market price and yield. Simple and free - works on any Android phone, no login, low data. Responsible AI - includes disclaimers "Confirm with local extension officers" and "Evidence & Limitations".

Intended impact: In Uganda 80% of people depend on farming but many plant maize yearly, degrading soil. With climate change, wrong crop choice means hunger. RotaUganda turns NASA satellite data into local action, supporting climate adaptation, soil health, food security as it scales to upto 1.5M smallholder farmers in Northern Uganda.

Tools used: Frontend -Next.js, Typescript is used full-stack. Backend - NASA POWER API - PRECTOTCORR and T2M daily point data, live calls. Hosting - Vercel. Rotation logic - Custom rule-based engine. No hardware needed.

Creativity: Instead of generic advice, we link live NASA weather to local rotation logic. Most apps use static data - ours is live per location. Anti-monocrop enforcement blocks same crop planting, directly answering "Don't Plant the Same". Tagline "Don't plant the same. Plant what comes next."

Factors considered: Climate reality -8% drier +1.1°C hotter, soil science, farmer reality - low literacy, low data, small phones, local trust in extension officers, poverty - most small holder farmers cannot afford fertilizer, scalability - 10 zones now design allows all Uganda.
